text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — eu-dedicated-cluster-03 is reporting elevated 5xx rates affecting Clearwave Health contact-routing. 30% of requests failing since 14:03 UTC. Impact: failed contact handoffs and delayed outbound notifications to Clearwave subaccounts. On-call: @raj (oncall). Runbook: contacts-routing-fallback.

raj (oncall): Ack. I’m on it. Starting triage now. @kevin can you pull logs for the routing service and check the KV cache hit rates?

kevin (sre): On it. Seeing a surge in backend 502s from route-service pod group rs-03. KV cache miss rate jumped to ~48% at spike. Logs show repeated errors calling backend-auth-service:
```
[14:03:12] route-service ERROR backend-auth-service: upstream timeout (504) - req_id=abc123
[14:03:15] route-service ERROR backend-auth-service: upstream timeout (504) - req_id=abc124
```
Likely origin is auth upstream in eu region. I’ve scaled route-service up x2 and toggled a short-term retry backoff.

elaine (acctmgr): FYI this is hitting our enterprise customer Clearwave Health. They have three main routing targets: cw-prod, cw-billing, cw-portal. Need a customer-facing impact statement and list of affected endpoints so I can notify their operations and account execs. Also, who owns the contact email list?

sam (support): I have their contact list in support CRM: primary ops: ops@clearwave.health, billing: billing@clearwave.health, tech lead: techlead@clearwave.health. Should we send a mass outage note or targeted per-account routing note?

lisa (eng-incident-lead): Suggest targeted. For cw-billing we should be explicit about delayed invoice notifications. For cw-prod and cw-portal, say "intermittent failures and elevated latency for contact routing and notifications". Draft statuspage + customer notice below — use placeholders we can paste into status page and email.

lisa (eng-incident-lead): PROPOSED STATUSPAGE (short):
```
Title: Degraded contact routing for Clearwave Health (eu-dedicated-cluster-03)
Impact: Intermittent failures and elevated latency for contact routing and notification delivery for Clearwave Health accounts.
Affected customers: Clearwave Health (cw-prod, cw-billing, cw-portal)
Start time: 2026-03-15 14:03 UTC
Current status: Investigating
Next update: +30m or when mitigated
```

lisa (eng-incident-lead): PROPOSED CUSTOMER EMAIL (targeted):
```
Subject: [Clearwave Health] Temporary disruption to contact routing - investigating
Hi <Customer Ops>,
We’re investigating an issue affecting contact routing and notification delivery for Clearwave Health (cw-prod, cw-billing, cw-portal) starting at ~14:03 UTC. You may see intermittent failures or delays in contact handoffs and notification delivery.
What we’re doing: Our on-call SREs have scaled the routing service, and we’re working with the upstream auth backend to restore normal traffic.
Estimated impact: Partial failures to deliver notifications and delayed routing for some traffic.
Next steps: We’ll send updates via this channel and the status page. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or contact Elaine (elaine@redwood.com) / Support (support@redwood.com).
Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a post-incident summary.
```

sam (support): I’ll prep the ticket and send the targeted email to ops@clearwave.health and techlead@clearwave.health. Elaine, can you confirm we should include execs?

elaine (acctmgr): Include the exec on standby: jason.exec@clearwave.health. Also cc: my team elaine@redwood.com and amanda.sa@redwood.com. Use the targeted template. Keep wording factual and non-technical.

kevin (sre): Quick mitigation note: adding short-term fallback routing rule to send requests to eu-fallback-01 when upstream-auth returns 5xx for 3 consecutive requests. Applying now:
```
kubectl apply -f fallback-rule-clearwave.yaml
# fallback-rule sets retry=1 and routes to eu-fallback-01
```
I’ll monitor error rate for 10m. If success, we can push a status update: "mitigation applied, partial recovery observed".

raj (oncall): Applied check to $ metrics: error rate down from 30% -> 12% after fallback. Latency still elevated for some paths. Keeping on-call.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to high. Paging sequence updated. Notifying account execs as requested.

lisa (eng-incident-lead): Customer-facing statusblock ready — Sam/ELAINE please review before posting. Small phrasing tweak: replace "partial failures" with "intermittent failures".

sam (support): Updated and queued. I’ll post to status.redwood.com and send targeted emails. Posting now.

sam (support): Status page posted: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1978642000 — message: "Mitigation applied; partial recovery; intermittent failures may continue for affected Clearwave subaccounts."

elaine (acctmgr): Sent targeted email to ops@clearwave.health, techlead@clearwave.health, billing@clearwave.health, cc jason.exec@clearwave.health, elaine@redwood.com, amanda.sa@redwood.com. Customer replies will go to support thread ID T-99823.

kevin (sre): Monitoring 10m window. Error rate trending down to ~5%. Will validate auth upstream for root cause.

ops-rotation: FYI @raj — I’ll take handoff at 20:00 UTC tonight. Please record current status and handoff notes in the incident doc:
- mitigation: fallback rule applied to route to eu-fallback-01
- impact: intermittent contact-routing failures for Clearwave Health subaccounts (cw-prod, cw-billing, cw-portal)
- customer comms: status page + targeted email sent to ops and execs
- next steps: confirm upstream-auth fix or rollback to stable version; run post-incident RCA

raj (oncall): Handback noted. I’ll add timeframe and link to logs in the incident doc and assign RCA owners. If error rate creeps up >10% re-alert.

lisa (eng-incident-lead): Thanks team. Good coordination. Keep updates compact in thread. I’ll start post-incident summary draft.

incident-bot: Incident auto-update scheduled at +30m. If resolved earlier, mark resolved with resolution summary. :white_check_mark:
